data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The critical distinction is not merely 'safe = read-only, idempotent = convergent under repetition,' but rather that RFC 9110 safety carries a client-expectation dimension: a safe method is one where 'the client does not request, and does not expect, any state change.' Idempotence carries no such expectation \u2014 the client expects a state change but expects it to be invariant under duplication. For the event log, this client-expectation dimension is decisive: writers always expect and request a state change (append), so safety is categorically impossible regardless of deduplication strategy. The log requires idempotence because writers expect mutation but must tolerate delivery duplication.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110 \u00a79.2.1 does not include the 'client does not request/expect' language and defines safety purely as server-side no-mutation, the client-expectation framing collapses to the simpler read-only distinction","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the event-log writer is modeled as a system-internal component (not an HTTP client), the client-expectation dimension of RFC 9110 safety may not apply at all, making the distinction moot for this context","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"RFC 9110 \u00a79.2.1 defines safety as not merely 'no side effect' but as a contract involving client intent: the client does not expect state change. This is stronger than a purely server-side 'no mutation' property. A writer to an append-only log, by definition, requests a state change (the append), so even if deduplication makes the second attempt a no-op, the writer's first attempt is a mutation request, violating the client-expectation component of safety. Idempotence has no such client-expectation constraint \u2014 it only constrains the server's response to repetition.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
